About.story1: Weiyon Industry began as a small machining workshop in central Taiwan in the 1980s — when Taiwan's manufacturing sector was just taking off, and every process still relied on the senior machinist's hands-on judgment. Our origins reflect that era: starting with a drawing, a piece of stock, and a set of files.
About.story2: Over four decades, the industry transformed many times. CNC machines replaced conventional lathes; semiconductors, aerospace, and medical became new customer markets; materials expanded from stainless steel and aluminum to titanium and other difficult-to-machine alloys. We changed with it — from the nervousness of installing our first CNC mill to the confidence of running complex multi-axis paths today, every upgrade carried hours of relentless learning.
About.story3: But some things never changed. Daily machine checks before startup. A measurement record for every dimension. A batch number traceable on every piece of material. These seemingly old-fashioned disciplines are how we keep our promise on quality. When customers order, they receive more than parts — they receive 40 years of uncompromising commitment.
About.story4: Today's Weiyon Industry is built on the same conviction: get every part right. From one-off prototypes to volume production, from Taiwan-domestic to overseas orders, from traditional mechanical parts to advanced semiconductor components — no matter the size of the project, we treat every drawing as if it were our first.

Workflow.metaTitle: Workflow — From Inquiry to Shipment in 5 Steps
Workflow.metaDescription: Weiyon Industry's CNC precision machining workflow: inquiry, quote, prototype, production, delivery — five clear stages. Each stage spells out what you do and what we do, with realistic timelines.
Workflow.heroTitle:
From Inquiry to Shipment
Five Clear Stages
Workflow.heroSubtitle: Each stage lays out what you do, what we do, and how long it takes — no guesswork.
Workflow.step1Description: Send us drawings, specs, quantity, and target lead time. No drawings? We can reverse-engineer from a sample.
Workflow.step1Your: Send drawings (DWG / DXF / PDF / STEP / IGES), material, quantity, surface finish requirements
Workflow.step1Ours: Respond within 1-2 business days, follow up by phone if details need confirming
Workflow.step2Description: The quote includes unit and total prices, lead time, materials, and processes — so you have everything you need to compare and decide.
Workflow.step2Your: Review quote, adjust specs, confirm requirements
Workflow.step2Ours: Provide a detailed quotation; revise immediately when needs change
Workflow.step3Description: Prototyping de-risks production. For direct production or urgent orders, we can skip to step 4.
Workflow.step3Your: Test the sample, share modification feedback
Workflow.step3Ours: Machine the prototype to drawing, measure, and deliver with measurement reports
Workflow.step4Description: Formal production scheduling with continuous quality control — incoming inspection, in-process monitoring, periodic sampling.
Workflow.step4Ours: Schedule production, report progress regularly, document QC throughout
Workflow.step5Description: Final inspection, packaging, and shipping. Inspection reports available; packaging per your spec.
Workflow.step5Ours: Final inspection, packaging (rust / shock prevention), shipping per agreed method

Workflow.leadTimeFootnote: Above is a typical reference. Actual lead times depend on material stock, machining complexity, surface treatment scope, and current shop load. Final lead time per formal quote. Holiday periods (Lunar New Year etc.) announced separately.
Workflow.prepTitle: How to get your quote faster
Workflow.prepSubtitle: With these 4 items in hand, we typically reply within 1-2 business days. Incomplete info is fine too — we'll just need a few rounds to confirm specs, which extends the timeline.

Workflow.prepTip: It's OK if you can't fill all fields — just send what you have, we'll ask for what's missing. The most common gaps are 'no drawing' or 'no material spec' — but if you have photos or a sample, we can reverse-engineer.
